newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Ruling Socialists win in Belgrade poll - official.
newsitem.headline: Ruling Socialists win in Belgrade poll - official.

text.p: Belgrade's electoral commission on Sunday awarded victory in the capital at a November local election to the ruling Socialist Party (SPS) and its ally the Yugoslav United Left (JUL) despite opposition claims of vote fraud.
"SPS and JUL won 66 seats, Zajedno (opposition coalition) 32, Serbian Radical Party 10 and Democratic Party of Serbia two," Commission President Radomir Lazarevic told a news conference.

The ruling of the City Electoral Commission came one day after the Supreme Court of Serbia decided to reject appeals by the Zajedno coalition which had claimed it had won more than 60 seats in the 110-seat city assembly and accused the Socialists of election fraud.

However, Lazarevic said the Commission had appealed to higher bodies -- the Yugoslav Federal Supreme Court, the Federal Public Prosecutor and the Serbian Public Prosecutor, to re-examine the Serbian Supreme Court's ruling "finding that the law has been violated in this instance".

"This does not mean necessarily that we are right. This means that the rule of law does exist in this country and must be respected," he said. All three legal bodies must respond within 48 hours, he said.
